content.value: A Project is the tenancy unit nested under a Workspace — the scope that bounds mutations, webhooks, and edge-projector rebuilds.
Where a Workspace is the outer tenant boundary, a Project is the unit inside it. In Barkpark production each Workspace carries one Project: the default workspace
. Together Workspace + Project form the full tenancy key that every Document and Dataset is filed under in the Content Model.
The Project is the scope that bounds the write and propagation paths:

items.value: are applied within a single Project — a write never crosses the boundary.
fire per Project, so a tenant's subscribers only hear about their own content changes (driving Cache Revalidation downstream).
run per Project, recomputing the Content Edges Table for just that tenant's slice of the Content Graph.

content.value: This keeps the Blue Green Rebuild cycle and Graph Traversal cleanly partitioned: one Project's orphans and dangling references never bleed into another's.

The Project travels with Auth and Tokens on the HTTP API v1 and, like the Workspace, contributes to the tier-keying of the Capabilities Manifest. The bp CLI and JS SDK both carry the Project in their configured context. Reads filtered by Perspective and body content carried as a PortableDoc are likewise bounded by the Project — the inner ring of the tenancy key.
